documents.inputText:
Karen yawned. Long nights in nursing were bad enough, but on a psych ward rotation, it was made worse by the instability of some of the patients. The flickering fluorescent lights overhead seemed to highlight all the worn out, worried, or scared looking faces in front of her. Some of them were loud, some were quiet, but most of them were completely alone in their own thoughts. 

Of course, the old hands on the ward were helping to shield her from some of the crazier ones. They had taken her under their wing and shown her the ropes. They taught her how to recognize the signs of a patient getting anxious, or of someone who was about to blow up, and most importantly, how to stay safe.

The alarms started going off. That was when she heard her name being called. "Code orange, two, code orange, two." Someone was in crisis. Someone was about to hurt themselves. Karen turned to leave, but her mentor was right behind her. "Stay close to me, Karen. Let's go take care of this."

 They got to the room and the door was locked. The nurse had to open it with a key. Inside, there was a girl sitting on the floor, her head against the wall. She was crying, really crying. She was begging for someone to stop her. "Don't do this," the nurse said. "You don't have to do this." But she did. She did do it. 

The next morning, there was a meeting. The doctor said, "Someone killed Sarah." "What are you talking about?" one of the nurses asked. "We don't know," the doctor said. "But it was someone here in the hospital. We don't know how, but someone stopped her from killing herself and now she is dead." 

 "Was it you," the doctor said, looking at one of the new nurses. "No," he said.
